newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Duisenberg says he assumes EMU will start on time.
newsitem.headline: Duisenberg says he assumes EMU will start on time.

text.p: Dutch central bank president Wim Duisenberg said on Friday he assumed European economic and monetary union would start on time, even though some countries were having trouble meeting the entry criteria.
Duisenberg takes over on July 1 as head of the European Monetary Institute, the forerunner of the European Central Bank, which is scheduled to run monetary policy under EMU from 1999.
Asked if he believed EMU would start on time in January 1999, he told reporters: "I'm working on that (assumption)."
Duisenberg rejected suggestions that the recent appointment of a Socialist-led government in France and Germany's budgetary problems could force a delay in the single currency project.
He noted that former French Socialist president Francois Mitterrand and former EU Commission president Jacques Delors, also a French socialist, had been staunch advocates of EMU.

Duisenberg said he did not believe Germany's recent decision not to use the proceeds of a revaluation of gold reserves to improve its 1997 budget position would adversely affect its prospects of meeting the EMU entry criteria on time.
